literal: In the ninth month, on dingwei, the moon transgressed the left Horn.
idiomatic: On dingwei in the ninth month the Moon crossed the eastern Horn star.

literal: The prognostication states: "The lord of men has anxiety."
idiomatic: The sovereign was warned of personal peril.

literal: One reading says: "The general of the left guard dies; under Heaven there are troops."
idiomatic: Another gloss added the death of the Left Guard general and nationwide war.

literal: In the second year, fourth month, on guiyou, the Year Star was seen in daytime.
idiomatic: On guiyou in the fourth month of Yongning 2 Jupiter appeared in daylight.

literal: The prognostication states: "Ministers are strong."
idiomatic: It warned that subjects would overpower their ruler.

literal: Earlier, Prince of Qi, Jiong, had pacified the capital and therefore remained to assist the government, whereupon he monopolized arrogance and had no ruler.
idiomatic: Earlier Sima Jiong had rescued Luoyang and stayed on as regent, growing insolent and treating the emperor as a cipher.

literal: In that month Chengdu and Hejian issued proclamations summoning Prince of Changsha, Yi, to campaign against him; Jiong and Yi fought, attacking and burning palace gates; Jiong’s army was defeated and exterminated root and branch.
idiomatic: That month the princes of Chengdu and Hejian called on Sima Yi of Changsha to attack Jiong; their armies clashed, torched the palaces, and annihilated Jiong’s host.

literal: They also killed his elder brother the Upper Army general Shi and more than twenty others below him.
idiomatic: They slew his elder brother Sima Shi, Upper Army general, and over twenty of his kin and lieutenants.

literal: In the second year of Taian, Chengdu attacked Changsha; thereby public and private suffered hunger and exhaustion; the common people’s strength was bent.
idiomatic: In Taian 2 the Prince of Chengdu besieged the Prince of Changsha, plunging court and countryside into famine and utter exhaustion.

literal: In the second month of the second year of Taian the Great White entered Net.
idiomatic: In Taian 2’s second month Venus entered the Net asterism.

literal: The prognostication states: "Under Heaven is disturbed; troops rise on a great scale."
idiomatic: The realm would convulse in great war.

literal: In the seventh month Spark-Delusion entered the Eastern Well.
idiomatic: In July Mars entered the Eastern Well.

literal: The prognostication states: "Troops rise; the state is in chaos."
idiomatic: Arms and civil disorder were portended.

literal: That autumn the Great White guarded the Supreme Minister in the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
idiomatic: That autumn Venus stationed on the Supreme Palace’s Supreme Minister star.

literal: The prognostication states: "The supreme minister perishes by arms."
idiomatic: It foretold the chief minister’s death in fighting.

literal: That winter Chengdu and Hejian attacked Luoyang.
idiomatic: That winter the armies of Chengdu and Hejian struck toward Luoyang.

literal: In the eighth month the Prince of Changsha led the emperor out to oppose the two princes.
idiomatic: In August Sima Yi of Changsha marched the sovereign out to face the allied princes.

literal: In the first month of the third year Prince of the East Sea, Yue, seized Prince of Changsha, Yi, and Zhang Fang again killed him.
idiomatic: In the third year’s first month Sima Yue of the East Sea captured Sima Yi of Changsha, whereupon Zhang Fang put him to death.

literal: In the first month of the third year Spark-Delusion entered the Southern Dipper; the prognostication is the same as Yongkang.
idiomatic: That same January Mars re-entered the Southern Dipper—the Yongkang omen applied again.

literal: In the seventh month the Left Guard general Chen Zhen led the host in attendance on the emperor to campaign against Chengdu; the six armies were utterly defeated; troops pressed the imperial carriage.
idiomatic: In July Left Guard commander Chen Zhen escorted the emperor against the Prince of Chengdu; the six hosts were routed and rebels closed on the imperial train.

literal: At this time bandits and rebels under Heaven rose in swarms; Zhang Chang was especially flourishing.
idiomatic: Rebels sprang up everywhere, Zhang Chang’s horde foremost among them.

literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Yongxing, on gengshen, the Great White transgressed Horn and Neck, passing through Room and Heart, traversing Tail and Winnowing Basket.
idiomatic: On gengshen in Yongxing 1’s seventh month Venus cut through Horn, Neck, Room, Heart, Tail, and the Winnowing Basket in succession.
